titre: Perspectives and the board of cards
changements: Perspectives: choose in the header what you see. Product shows a project's board, stories, backlog, what to test, roadmap, releases and requests; Administration shows production, delivery, activity, the log and setup; All keeps every tab. A perspective hides tabs, it never removes a right; a Product Engineer starts in Product.

Each project has a Board: cards written in La Fabrique, before they become stories (if ever). A card is a title and a few lines of Markdown, with a type (feature, idea, question), a status (draft, shaping, to validate, validated, dropped) and the project's own epic, domain, segment and release.

Arrange the board by one dimension, then by another to cross them (domains in columns, segments in rows), and filter it; the arrangement stays on this device. Drag a card by its handle (or Space and the arrow keys): it takes the values of the place it is dropped in. A new column creates a new value.

In a card's text, {segment: pro} sets a tag, #12 links an issue, @login names a person and [[Basket]] marks a term. Every version of a card is kept, every decision is in the project's log, and every card can be exported as JSON.

titre: Report a defect from the project's app
changements: A project's app reports a defect from the page where it shows up: La Fabrique opens the issue with the page, version, component and screenshot, labels it bug, links it to the story on int when there is one, and signs it with the person's login.
Anyone whose GitHub account sees the project can report, a role or not; reports from an account without a role are labelled to triage. At most 20 a day per account.
Reports are accepted only from an environment declared with signalement in .fabrique.json and that says it is that environment; Setup warns when an environment answers another one than its type.
Rights now follow one ladder: each role can do what the ones below it do (a tech lead can validate on int).

A project's own app can connect to La Fabrique in the name of the person using it, after a consent page (“‹app› will be able to report defects in your name on ‹project›”); it never gets a GitHub token.
Settings → Connected apps lists the apps you connected, with a button to disconnect each; the super admin registers a project's app there and gets its identifiers once.
An account without a role can sign in to connect an app, for a project whose repository it can see on GitHub; the rest of La Fabrique still turns it away.
Setup says whether the project has a promotion workflow (for the go) and a Claude workflow (for Launch Claude), what they need, and shows the épicerie's as examples.

Tech leads and super admins launch Claude on a ready story from the Backlog: La Fabrique starts the project's own Claude workflow with the issue number, labels the story ready for Claude and says so on the issue.
A cap of Claude runs at once per project (2 unless the project says otherwise); each launch is in the log.
When production is ready, the super admin gives the go from the Production tab: it shows the stories production will get and who validated each, then starts the project's own promotion workflow.
Stories not validated on int need a reason to go anyway; the go, its reason and the promotion run are kept and shown to everyone.

A Log tab: every decision taken in La Fabrique on a project, newest first, in words and with links to GitHub: requests written, criteria checked, stories validated, defects reported, priorities set, setup changes proposed.
Filter by kind of decision and by person; nothing in it can be changed or deleted.
La Fabrique has a logo: a sawtooth-roofed workshop, also in the browser tab.
With several projects, the project's name in the header opens a menu to switch to another one, on the same tab.
Links to GitHub and to the projects' environments open in a new tab.
On To test, testers, Product Engineers and super admins tick each acceptance criterion: it is ticked in the GitHub issue too.
Validate a story once every criterion is checked: the issue gets a comment with the int version, the to-validate label goes, and La Fabrique keeps who validated and when.
Report a defect from a story: it becomes a GitHub issue linked to the story, listed under it until fixed.
What La Fabrique writes in a project follows its language (langue in .fabrique.json).

titre: Change the story lifecycle from Setup
changements: Setup has a Story lifecycle section: the Definition of Ready checks and the priority labels, read from the project's .fabrique.json.

Super admins and tech leads propose a change from there: La Fabrique opens a pull request on the project, under their GitHub name, that changes only the lifecycle; the project reviews and merges it as usual.

The home page is now a dashboard: one card per project with what needs attention now (to test on int, production ready or not, in development and stalled work, ready to start, top priority in the backlog, CI on production, versions, last release), each figure leading to its tab.
What your role looks at comes first: testers see what to test, tech leads the CI and the work in progress, super admins production.
A Backlog tab: the stories not started yet, by priority, the ready ones first, each with its epic and what its Definition of Ready lacks.
Super admins, tech leads and Product Engineers set a story's priority from the backlog: La Fabrique puts the priority label on GitHub and writes who changed it in its log.
The project tabs keep to one line.

An In development tab: every story being worked on, with its branches, its pull request (draft or not), the CI result of its latest run and its last commit; work without a commit for 3 days is marked stalled.
Working branches that refer to no story are listed apart, with how to link them.

A To test tab answers "what is new on int?": the stories waiting on int, by epic, each with its acceptance criteria as a checklist, the release-notes changes production does not have yet, and a button to open int.
Without an integration branch, it says what the latest production version brought.
On a phone, the tabs scroll sideways on one line.
Each story has a stage on the Stories board: Backlog, Ready, In development, On int or In production, computed from GitHub, with a stage filter.
A story in the backlog says what its Definition of Ready lacks; each project declares its own Definition of Ready and priority labels in its .fabrique.json (Setup explains how).
Delivery shows at once, then fills in as GitHub answers, instead of a long wait on the first view; the workflows are read side by side.
The loading light has a hot orange core.
The red loading light now shows on older browsers too.
Pages keep following one another in place even when the host adds a script of its own to them.
Settings says whether pages follow in place on this device, and which browser it is.

titre: The red light keeps moving, Safari included
changements: La Fabrique now reads the next page itself while the current one stays on screen, so the red loading light keeps sweeping until the page is there, in Safari too.
Back and forward work as before; a page that needs its own script is still loaded by the browser.
A Settings page: the version online, and whether this device runs the latest stylesheet and script.
Reload everything: the browser forgets what it kept of La Fabrique, and the page comes back from the server; your session stays.
Try a slow page, to see the loading bar at work.
After each update, pages use the new styles and scripts at once, without waiting for the browser's copy to expire.

titre: A red scanner while pages load
changements: The loading bar is now a red light sweeping back and forth, and it keeps moving while the next page is on its way.
A Setup tab on each project: what La Fabrique needs to follow it well, read from its files and GitHub, each item done, missing or optional, with how to do it and an example.
An integration branch is optional; the Setup tab explains how to add one.
La Fabrique serves its own .fabrique.json and release-notes format, which the how-to links open.

The Production tab opens on what production will get: the stories the pending work refers to, by epic, and every release-notes entry production does not have yet, with a count of stories, versions and changes.
Choose a project's reference branch from a menu in the header, with a search over all its branches; like a checkout, it stays chosen on every tab until you go back to production.
Production compares the chosen branch with production; Activity, Delivery, Releases, Roadmap and the documentation read that branch.
The project, its branch and who you are now share one compact line under the bar.
A thin bar runs at the top of the page while the next one loads.
La Fabrique extraordinaire can be added as a project of its own: its documentation, stories, delivery, activity and releases show like any other project's.
The version endpoint gives the version number as well as the deployed commit.
A Roadmap tab: a month calendar of versions released, stories closed and epics done, and each epic's progress day by day.
A Releases tab: every version's notes by day, with the stories closed since the previous version.
A Delivery tab: each workflow's runs over 30 days, share passed, median duration, current streak and last failure.

titre: Read a project on another branch
changements: A branch selector on a project's page: read its documentation and its .fabrique.json on integration or a working branch, production staying the reference.
An Activity tab: commits and lines changed per day over 30 or 90 days, and commits per author.
Product Engineers, tech leads and super admins write a request from the project's own form; it becomes an issue under their name.
Drafts stay on the device until the request is sent; My requests shows where each one stands.
A Production tab: the work on integration missing from production, grouped by merged branch, with versions, workflows and a clear ready or not ready.
A Stories tab: issues grouped by epic, with their state, labels, pull requests and branches, and filters.
A project's documentation reads in La Fabrique, from its production branch, with links between pages kept inside.
The app is now called La Fabrique extraordinaire.
Super admins add a project from the repositories where the GitHub App is installed; its .fabrique.json is checked, with readable errors.
Sign in with GitHub; only people given a role get in, and super admins manage roles on the People page.
La Fabrique is online, with its home page.
